title: Three observations from timing and auditing the mesher: thread safety, what Timings reports, and the certificate near the axis
body: **What we found.** Three things, from timing and auditing `cube_mesh` and `scroll_whole` on Linux over a 27 cube window and a 1,728 cube window of PHerc. 0139. The vendored f2c layer keeps its state in `static` locals, so two cubes cannot unwrap at once. The `Timings` line names about a tenth of a cube. The winding certificate is evaluated inside the umbilicus, where its own angle is undefined. Where a cube's time goes, with the growth gate off and on. The Timings line the tool prints names about a tenth of what the cube takes. **Why it matters.** The shipped default for `--max-concurrent` is 32, so anyone running the tool as documented on more than one cube meets the first. The second invites a wrong conclusion about where a cube's time goes. The third makes a count mean less than a reader takes it to mean. **That none of this is urgent and none is a claim about your results.** Each of the three is a measurement of the tool's behaviour on our machine with a control beside it, and no delivered sheet is said to be wrong anywhere in this issue. The one finding that does bear on a delivered sheet is in a separate issue. **The numbers**, one row per cube where a cube is the unit: | cube | total | named by `Timings` | share | |---|---:|---:|---:| | z09216_y03840_x03840 | 845.900 s | 75.972 s | 8.98 % | | z09472_y02560_x02560 | 417.374 s | 50.698 s | 12.15 % | | z09728_y03712_x02560 | 498.311 s | 58.020 s | 11.64 % | For the concurrency: 27 cubes at `--max-concurrent 4` abort in 3 s, 9 cubes at 3 give `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`, and 9 cubes at 1 return rc 0 in 76.0 s. For the certificate: of the 118 faces it rejects over the 1,728 cube window, 71 have their centroid below one voxel from the axis, between r = 0.0539 and r = 0.4895, and 45 are at 500 voxels or more. That is 60 per cent of the count coming from inside the umbilicus. **How to check it yourself.** Run `scroll_whole` on nine cubes at `--max-concurrent 3` and then at 1. Sum the `Timings` line of one cube and compare it with the cube's own wall clock. Audit a meshed window with the axis table attached and sort the rejected faces by the distance of their centroid from the axis. --- We timed and audited `cube_mesh` and `scroll_whole` on Linux, on a 27 cube window and a 1,728 cube window of PHerc0139. Three things came out that are worth writing down and none of them is urgent. A fourth, which is, is in a separate issue. ## 1. The vendored f2c layer keeps its state in `static` locals, so two cubes cannot unwrap at once `deps/taucs/external/src/genmmd.c` has static integer mdeg, ehead, i, mdlmt, mdnode; and the mmd helpers do the same. Two cubes entering the ordering routine at the same time corrupt the heap. Measured: | concurrency | outcome | |---|---| | 27 cubes at `--max-concurrent 4` | abort in 3 s | | 9 cubes at 3 | `free(): double free detected in tcache 2` | | 9 cubes at 1 | rc 0 in 76.0 s | We run `scroll_whole` with `--max-concurrent 1`, which is a serialisation and not a fix, and it gives up the whole parallelism of the assembly. **The shipped default is 32**, so anyone running the tool as documented on more than one cube meets this. ## 2. The `Timings` line names about a tenth of a cube on the arm we ship We built a stage map of three grid cubes with the growth gate armed, accounting for 99.95 to 99.97 per cent of the wall clock. Against that, the `Timings` line reports: | cube | total | named by `Timings` | share | |---|---:|---:|---:| | z09216_y03840_x03840 | 845.900 s | 75.972 s | **8.98 %** | | z09472_y02560_x02560 | 417.374 s | 50.698 s | **12.15 %** | | z09728_y03712_x02560 | 498.311 s | 58.020 s | **11.64 %** | So **87.8 to 91.0 per cent of a cube is not in that line.** This is not a bug, and we raise it for one reason: it invites a wrong conclusion about where the time goes, and we drew one ourselves before building the map. It may also be part of why profiles of this tool disagree. Issue #3 measures MLS at about 83 per cent of wall clock on a 320 cubed Kaggle cube at `--halo 0 --no-qem`; on the grid cubes we ship, with the gate armed and QEM on, we measure Resplit at 85.39 to 88.96 per cent and Extract at 7.48 to 9.92. **Neither refutes the other. Which stage dominates depends on the cube and the flags**, and a `Timings` line that named the whole cube would make that visible to everybody at once. ## 3. The winding certificate is evaluated inside the umbilicus, where its own angle is undefined Over the 1,728 cubes of a twelve cube window, gate armed at 0.45, audited with the axis table attached the way `cube_mesh` attaches it, the certificate rejects **118 faces**. By the distance of the face centroid from the axis: | radius | faces | |---|---:| | **below 1 voxel** | **71** | | 1 to 100 | 0 | | 100 to 500 | 2 | | 500 or more | 45 | The 71 lie between r = 0.0539 and r = 0.4895 voxels. At that distance the angle of a position about the axis is not meaningful and a winding difference computed from it is not either. **Sixty per cent of what the certificate reports on this window comes from inside the umbilicus.** A floor on the radius, or an exclusion, would make the remaining count mean what a reader takes it to mean. We are happy to post the per face table.
